title: Lesson 17: لَام التَّعْلِيل and أَنْ الْمَصْدَرِيَّة — Giving a Reason and Turning a Verb into a Noun
summary: After finishing the مَا exercises, the class takes up the two constructions that run through lesson seventeen. لَام التَّعْلِيل supplies the reason for an action and puts the following مُضَارِع into the accusative — خَرَجْتُ لِأَشْرَبَ الْمَاءَ. أَنْ الْمَصْدَرِيَّة does the same to the verb's ending but also converts it in meaning into a مَصْدَر, so that أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَجْلِسَ amounts to أُرِيدُ الْجُلُوسَ — in practice, the English to.
key_points: مَا الْمَوْصُولَة never changes form, whatever the gender or number of what it refers to, whereas الَّذِي has الَّتِي، الَّذِينَ and the rest.

لَام التَّعْلِيل (lām al-taʿlīl) gives the reason for the verb before it, so it generally sits between two verbs: خَرَجْتُ لِأَشْرَبَ الْمَاءَ، خَرَجَ لِيَغْسِلَ وَجْهَهُ. It puts the following مُضَارِع into the accusative — لِأَشْرَبَ, not لِأَشْرَبُ.
لِأَنَّ also means because but is the more general word, and it is normally followed by a noun rather than a verb.
أَنْ الْمَصْدَرِيَّة (an al-maṣdariyyah) has four properties: it follows a verb, a مُضَارِع verb comes after it, it puts that verb into the accusative, and it gives it the meaning of a مَصْدَر.

So أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَجْلِسَ هُنَا is equivalent in sense to أُرِيدُ الْجُلُوسَ هُنَا — I want to sit here. The most practical translation of أَنْ is simply the English to: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَذْهَبَ (I want to go), أُرِيدُ أَنْ آكُلَ (I want to eat).
This أَنْ, without a shadda, is a different word from أَنَّ, the sister of إِنَّ.

يُمْكِنُ means it is possible, and with a pronoun attached it carries the sense of can: يُمْكِنُهُ أَنْ يَجْلِسَ, he can sit. It is the verb behind the familiar إِمْكَان and مُمْكِن, and the polite way to ask permission — يُمْكِنُنِي أَنْ أَذْهَبَ إِلَى الْحَمَّامِ.
مُنْذُ (since) is a new حَرْف الجَرّ, so the word after it takes a kasra: غَائِبٌ مُنْذُ أُسْبُوعٍ.
غَائِب means absent — the same root as الْغَيْب, the unseen, but here simply not present.
بَدَأَ، يَبْدَأُ means to begin, so تَبْدَأُ الْعُطْلَةُ is the vacation starts.
مُقْبِل means coming or next, a synonym of قَادِم — الْعَام الْمُقْبِل, the coming year — and عَام is another word for year beside سَنَة.
رَجَا، يَرْجُو is to hope, giving أَرْجُو (I hope); سَمَحَ، يَسْمَحُ is to give permission — أَرْجُو أَنْ تَسْمَحَ لَنَا, I hope you will permit us.
هُدُوء is calmness, and بِهُدُوءٍ means calmly or quietly.
Vocabulary: عُطْلَة (vacation) with الصَّيْف (summer), قَمِيص (shirt), بَلَد (country), قَبُول (acceptance), and عِلَاج (medical treatment).
questions: [00:02:07] Q: Shouldn't it be the masculine آخَر, since خَبَر is masculine? — A: No, because what is being described is the radio station, which is feminine, so أُخْرَى is correct. The صِفَة follows the word it actually describes.
[00:06:00] Q: What is مَا الْمَوْصُولَة? — A: It means that or which, like الَّذِي, and unlike الَّذِي it keeps one form for singular, dual and plural, masculine and feminine alike.

[00:17:00] Q: How is this different from بِمَا and لِأَنَّ? — A: بِمَا means with what; لِأَنَّ means because and is general, usually followed by a noun; لَام التَّعْلِيل attaches to a verb and gives the reason for the action.
[00:20:00] Q: What does أُرِيدُ أَنْ mean? — A: I want to. The أَنْ turns the following verb into the sense of a مَصْدَر, so it reads as the English to.
[00:25:00] Q: Can someone remind us what a مَصْدَر is? — A: The noun form of a verb, naming the act itself, tied to no person or time.
[00:27:00] Q: Haven't we had أَنْ before? — A: That was أَنَّ with a shadda, the sister of إِنَّ. This أَنْ is a different word.
[00:29:11] Q: Is مُنْذُ a new word? — A: Yes, and it is a حَرْف الجَرّ meaning since, so the following word takes a kasra.
[00:30:00] Q: Is مُمْكِن an Arabic word, or only Urdu? — A: It is Arabic, the اسْم form of يُمْكِنُ, and it is used commonly in Urdu as well, as is إِمْكَان.

quiz.q: What does لَام التَّعْلِيل express, and where does it sit?
options: The reason for an action, generally between two verbs
quiz.a: تَعْلِيل is giving a cause: خَرَجْتُ لِأَشْرَبَ الْمَاءَ — I went out in order to drink water.

quiz.q: What does لَام التَّعْلِيل do to the verb after it?
quiz.a: أَشْرَبُ becomes لِأَشْرَبَ and يَغْسِلُ becomes لِيَغْسِلَ.

quiz.q: How does لِأَنَّ differ in use from لَام التَّعْلِيل?
options: لِأَنَّ is the general word for because and normally takes a noun after it
لِأَنَّ can only be used in questions
لِأَنَّ takes a command after it
quiz.a: The teacher distinguished them on exactly this point: لِأَنَّ is general and followed by an ism.

quiz.q: Which four things are true of أَنْ الْمَصْدَرِيَّة?
options: It follows a noun, takes a مَاضِي, gives a kasra, and negates
It follows a verb, takes a مُضَارِع, gives that verb a fatḥa, and lends it the meaning of a مَصْدَر
It begins a sentence, takes a مُضَارِع, gives a ḍamma, and asks a question
It follows a verb, takes a command, gives a sukūn, and prohibits
quiz.a: These were the four properties the teacher listed on the board.

quiz.q: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَجْلِسَ is equivalent in meaning to which phrase?
quiz.a: Because أَنْ gives the verb the force of a مَصْدَر, and الْجُلُوس is the مَصْدَر of جَلَسَ.

quiz.q: What is the simplest way to translate أَنْ in this construction?
quiz.a: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَذْهَبَ is I want to go — though the teacher cautioned it is a rule of thumb, not a blanket equivalence.

quiz.q: How does this أَنْ differ from أَنَّ?
options: They are different words: أَنَّ with the shadda is a sister of إِنَّ
أَنْ is used only in questions
أَنَّ takes a verb, أَنْ takes a noun
quiz.a: The teacher corrected this explicitly when a student connected the two.

quiz.q: What does يُمْكِنُهُ أَنْ يَجْلِسَ mean?
options: He can sit — literally, it is possible for him to sit
quiz.a: يُمْكِنُ means it is possible, and with an attached pronoun it carries the sense of can — the same root as إِمْكَان.

quiz.q: What kind of word is مُنْذُ, and what does it do?
options: A حَرْف الجَرّ meaning since, giving the next word a kasra
quiz.a: غَائِبٌ مُنْذُ أُسْبُوعٍ — absent for a week, with أُسْبُوع in the genitive.
هُدُوء is calmness, so بِهُدُوءٍ is calmly or quietly.

quran_examples.arabic: وَمَا هَٰذَا إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُكُمْ يَأْكُلُ مِمَّا تَأْكُلُونَ مِنْهُ وَيَشْرَبُ مِمَّا تَشْرَبُونَ
quran_examples.transliteration: wa-mā hādhā illā basharun mithlukum yaʾkulu mimmā taʾkulūna minhu wa-yashrabu mimmā tashrabūn
quran_examples.translation: And this is not but a man like yourselves. He eats of that from which you eat and drinks of what you drink.
quran_examples.note: The teacher's example while the class translated آكُلُ مَا تَأْكُلُ: مِمَّا is مِنْ with مَا الْمَوْصُولَة — that which you eat — and the āyah also opens with مَا النَّافِيَة, so two of the three types of مَا appear together.

quran_examples.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لِمَ تَقُولُونَ مَا لَا تَفْعَلُونَ
quran_examples.transliteration: yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū lima taqūlūna mā lā tafʿalūn
quran_examples.translation: O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do?
quran_examples.note: The sentence the class translated as why do you say that which you do not do: مَا الْمَوْصُولَة followed by لَا النَّافِيَة, with لِمَ as the short form of لِمَاذَا.

quran_examples.translation: I do not worship what you worship.
quran_examples.note: Read in the exercise as a further instance of مَا الْمَوْصُولَة, standing for objects of worship, which are غَيْر عَاقِل.

quran_examples.arabic: أَتُرِيدُ أَن تَقْتُلَنِي كَمَا قَتَلْتَ نَفْسًا بِالْأَمْسِ
quran_examples.transliteration: a-turīdu an taqtulanī kamā qatalta nafsan bi-l-ams
quran_examples.translation: Do you intend to kill me as you killed someone yesterday?
quran_examples.note: A Qur'ānic instance of exactly the construction of this lesson — أَرَادَ followed by أَنْ and a مُضَارِع in the accusative, تَقْتُلَنِي rather than تَقْتُلُنِي.

quran_examples.translation: Allah wishes to lighten your burden.
quran_examples.note: أَنْ الْمَصْدَرِيَّة again after يُرِيدُ, and يُخَفِّفَ is on the فَعَّلَ pattern introduced the previous week.

quran_examples.arabic: لِّيَغْفِرَ لَكَ اللَّهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِن ذَنبِكَ وَمَا تَأَخَّرَ
quran_examples.transliteration: li-yaghfira laka llāhu mā taqaddama min dhanbika wa-mā taʾakhkhar
quran_examples.translation: That Allah may forgive you what preceded of your sin and what will follow.
quran_examples.note: A clear Qur'ānic لَام التَّعْلِيل: يَغْفِرُ becomes لِيَغْفِرَ with the fatḥa, and مَا appears twice as الْمَوْصُولَة.

quran_examples.arabic: وَمَا خَلَقْتُ الْجِنَّ وَالْإِنسَ إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُونِ
quran_examples.transliteration: wa-mā khalaqtu al-jinna wa-l-insa illā li-yaʿbudūn
quran_examples.translation: And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me.
quran_examples.note: The lām of purpose again, answering why the act was done — the same function as لِأَشْرَبَ in the lesson's opening exchange.
